summary: Yoshihiko Nasu works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held appointments at Ryukoku University (attested 2007), Kongo Jushinkai (attested 2017), and Kongo-ju (attested 2017).

Yoshihiko Sakurai specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2001) and was later affiliated with Ryukoku University and the Kyogaku Dendo Research Center (both attested 2003).
Yoshihiro Hayashi specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. In 2009, he was attested as a part-time lecturer at both Ritsumeikan University and Shitennoji University.

Yoshihito Muroji works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg in 1992 under Lambert Schmithausen, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, later holding posts at Kyoto, Koyasan, and Shiga universities.
Yoshiki Motoaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He has been affiliated with Otani University (attested 2013) and the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

Yoshimi Nozawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. As of 2026, he is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Yoshinobu Kimoto is a historian and Japanologist who studied at Komazawa, Meiji, and Tezukayama universities. He held academic posts at Yamagata Prefectural Yonezawa Women's Junior College (1993–2000), Koshien Junior College (2000–2012), and Ryukoku University (2013–2021).
Yoshinobu Sakade (1934–2020) was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1953–1958) under Mitsuji Fukunaga and held a post at Kansai University from circa 1978 to 2005.

Yoshinori Takeuchi (1913–2002) studied philosophy, religion, and Buddhist studies at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe. He served as a professor at Kyoto University (1959–1976) and Aichi Gakuin University (~1977–1988), and joined the Japan Academy in 1995.

Yoshinori Yasuda (1946–2026) was an archaeologist and Japanologist. Educated at Ritsumeikan and Tohoku universities, he served at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~1988–2012), Tohoku University (~2012–2014), and Reitaku University (~2014).

Yoshio Kawakatsu (1922–1984) was a Sinologist and historian who studied at Kyoto University (~1945–1948) and under Paul Demiéville (~1967–1969). He spent his career on the library assistant staff at Kyoto University (~1952–1984).
Yoshio Nishiguchi is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.
Yoshio Takeuchi (1886–1966) was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1907–1910) and held a post at Tohoku University from circa 1923 to 1946.

Yoshiro Imaeda is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University. He worked at the CNRS (~1974–2012) and held positions with the National Library of Bhutan and Kyoto University.

Yoshiro Tamura (1921–1989) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University. He held professorships at Toyo University, the University of Tokyo, and Rissho University, and was a visiting professor at Chicago.

Yoshitaka Iriya (1910–1998) studied Sinology and Buddhist studies at Kyoto University under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He held academic posts at Kyoto University, Nagoya University, and Kyoto Sangyo University.
Yoshito S. Hakeda (1924–1983) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served on the faculty at Columbia University, where he taught until 1983.
Yoshitoyo Ohara works in the fields of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He was affiliated with Kyoto University (attested 2006) and Kyoto National Museum (attested 2016).

Yoshitsugu Sawai specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Tenri, Tohoku, and Harvard universities—completing his doctorate under John B. Carman—and served on the faculty at Tenri University from circa 1987 to 2017.

Yoshiyasu Yonezawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held appointments at Taisho University (attested 1998–2026) and at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
